description: E2E (fake Google OAuth, custom host serving both): technician clicks Google on the custom host's sign-in page; the authorize request carries the canonical redirect_uri; the user ends signed in on the custom host at the requested /msp path; password sign-in on the custom host still works in place
DB-backed: computeVanityRedirect for an internal-user token with a callback on the tenant's active 'both' domain issues an OTT row (with surface) and returns the custom host's handoff URL

DB-backed guards: no OTT and no handoff URL when the target domain belongs to another tenant, is not active, or is client_portal-only for an /msp return path; client-user handoff to a client_portal domain still works

DB-backed exchange for an internal user: consumes the OTT once, sets a session cookie whose decoded token equals what the shared minting function produces for a direct sign-in (plan/subscription claims included), redirects to the MSP return path; a second exchange of the same OTT fails
DB-backed exchange guards: OTT for another tenant's domain is refused; an /msp return path on a client_portal-only domain is refused
Provisioning: direct provisioner and the Temporal deployment-status activity move a 'both' domain to active once HTTPS/routing are ready, and write no sso_redirect_uris
DB-backed migration: pending_redirect_uri rows become active with sso_redirect_uris stripped; rows in other statuses are untouched
